title: UFC Qatar Official Scorecards Revealed: Full Fight Results & Analysis on UFC.com
body:
The UFC’s return to Doha on November 21, 2026 delivered a night of high‑octane action that will be remembered as one of the most tightly contested light‑heavyweight bouts in recent memory. Former champion Jiří Procházka faced rising star Navajo Stirling in a five‑round showdown that saw every round meticulously dissected by the three judges, ultimately resulting in a split‑decision victory for the Czech powerhouse. The official scorecards, released shortly after the fight, reveal just how razor‑thin the margin was and underscore the strategic chess match that unfolded inside the ABHA Arena.

From the opening bell, Prochazzka—still reeling from a year‑long layoff after his dramatic title loss—looked to re‑establish his reputation as a relentless finisher. He began aggressively, closing the distance with heavy leg kicks and a series of clinch‑driven knees that earned him the first round on two of the three cards (48‑47, 48‑47). Stirling, however, showcased the composure that has propelled him into the upper echelons of the division, counter‑striking with crisp jabs and a well‑timed overhand that landed cleanly in the second round. The second round was awarded unanimously to the Navajo fighter (49‑46 across the board), as he dictated pace, landed more significant strikes, and avoided Procházka’s grappling attempts.

Round three proved to be the pivotal swing in the contest. Procházka, sensing the need to assert dominance, intensified his pressure, securing a takedown and delivering a series of ground‑and‑pound strikes that appeared to sway the momentum. The judges were split: two scored it for the Czech veteran (48‑47), while the third gave the edge to Stirling, citing his continued striking volume and defensive acumen (48‑47). This divergence set the tone for the final two rounds, where both athletes traded control in a display of technical proficiency and heart.

The fourth round saw Stirling rebound with a flurry of body shots that visibly slowed Procházka’s forward motion. His footwork remained sharp, and he managed to avoid any further takedowns, prompting two judges to award him the round (49‑46). The final round was a war of attrition; Procházka, aware that the decision hung in the balance, unleashed a relentless barrage of punches and a last‑minute attempt at a standing guillotine that nearly ended the fight. Yet Stirling’s defensive resilience held firm, and he finished the bout with a series of clean strikes that earned him a unanimous 49‑46 from the panel.

When the scores were tallied, the official verdict read 48‑47, 48‑47 for Procházka and 48‑47 for Stirling, delivering a split‑decision win to the former champion. The narrow margin sparked immediate debate among analysts and fans alike, with many pointing to the subjective nature of octagon scoring—particularly in a fight where both combatants excelled in striking and grappling at different moments. The UFC’s own commentary team highlighted Procházka’s effective aggression and control on the ground, while also praising Stirling’s technical striking and defensive mastery throughout the encounter.

Beyond the immediate outcome, the fight carries broader implications for the light‑heavyweight division. Procházka’s victory repositions him as a legitimate contender for a title shot, potentially setting up a rematch with current champion Alexei “The Hammer” Petrov in early 2027. Meanwhile, Stirling’s performance solidifies his status as a top‑five contender, and his ability to edge a former champion on the judges’ cards may accelerate his ascent toward a championship bout. The split‑decision also reignites discussions about the UFC’s scoring criteria, prompting calls for greater transparency and perhaps a revisitation of the 10‑point must system to better reflect the multifaceted nature of modern mixed‑martial‑arts contests.

As the UFC continues to expand its global footprint, Doha’s successful hosting of this marquee event underscores the Middle East’s growing importance as a hub for premier combat‑sport spectacles. The enthusiastic local crowd, state‑of‑the‑art arena facilities, and seamless production value have set a benchmark for future events in the region. Looking ahead, fans can anticipate another high‑profile card in Doha later this year, with the promotion eyeing a heavyweight showdown that could further cement the city’s reputation as a premier destination for world‑class MMA.
